cross_capability_patterns.description: Explicit exclusion/negation of a named brand or product does not filter it out of retrieval - observed across 2 distinct capabilities (NEGATION, PRODUCT_SEARCH), 3 scenarios, both splits.

The generic 'which two products do you want to compare' clarification prompt fired for two completely unrelated query types (cuisine category discovery, login-method FAQ) that never mentioned comparison at all.
Rice-vinegar-specific requests (advice and replacement) both returned plain rice products instead of rice vinegar.

'What do I need from Foodland for X' phrasing (tom kha, pad thai) fell through to the generic zero-product bare-recipe redirect instead of the use_case_advice ingredient-role products, despite LIVE_USE_CASES covering both dishes.

BENCHMARK SELF-INTEGRITY FINDING (not an Advisor defect): several V2.20a expected_invariants used ASCII-only product_title_contains_any terms ('kokosove mlieko', 'omacka', 'sojova omacka') that structurally cannot match real catalog titles, which consistently carry Slovak diacritics ('kokosové', 'omáčka'). invariant_evaluator._lower() does not strip diacritics (confirmed by design during V2.18d.7/V2.19). At least 2-3 FAILs are very likely false negatives caused by this, not Advisor defects.

failures.classification_note: requires_uncertainty marker vocabulary is Slovak-only; the actual EN answer IS cautious in substance ('I don't want to recommend a product by name alone... check the label') but uses different phrasing my invariant doesn't recognize. Separately noted: the EN answer leaked the Slovak word 'alergény' mid-sentence - a real but low-severity mixed-language cosmetic defect.
